summary: Family Type's Universal Sans is not a specimen page but a one-screen, dark configurator app: a seven-step side panel lets the visitor build their own sans (six custom axes, per-glyph alternates, extra weights, italics, optical size, name), a big live sample with a toolbar previews it, and the build (encoded in a shareable BuildID URL) is downloaded as a trial or licensed in an on-page Stripe checkout. Phones get a static fallback page instead ('Visit on desktop').

instances.variantDefinition: A single-screen app where a numbered step panel walks the visitor through building their own version of the font (axis values, per-glyph alternates, extra weights, italics, optical size, name) while a large live sample previews every choice; the build is encoded in a shareable ID or URL and ends in a trial download or a licence purchase.
instances.look: Black app screen: huge white 'Hello font friend.' filling the left 3/4, a charcoal side panel at right headed '1. START HERE' with intro copy, BASIC | INTERPOLATOR pill tabs and slider rows (Weight 450, Width 50, X-height 40, Ink Traps 25…) each with a '?' button, a numbered step rail 1–7 on the far right edge, and a slim top bar with 'UNIVERSAL SANS 2.0' and the live 'BuildID v2.0.0.50.25.40.50.1111…450'
instances.feel: A design tool, not a brochure: calm, confident, empowering
instances.ux: Work down seven steps: 1 Geometry (six axis sliders or the XY interpolator), 2A–2C Alternates (pick numbered variants for a, a spur/tail, g, shoulder hn, y, terminal curve tfj, l, J, Q, R, G, K/k junction; numerals 1 2 3 7 6&9; round or square dots, curly or straight punctuation), 3 Add weights (+/– extra weights), 4 Add italics (9° slant, single-storey a option), 5 Optical size (Text, Display or both), 6 Name your typeface, 7 Download (trial or licence); every choice updates the sample and the BuildID in the URL hash so the build can be saved and shared
instances.learn: Turn the variable font's design space into a guided build-your-own-family flow: numbered steps, a '?' explanation for every option and a URL-encoded build ID make an open-ended configurator feel safe and finishable

reconstruction.layout: 1440×900 fixed app, no page scroll. Stage 0–1070px wide (sample top-left at x=20, y=80); side panel x=1070–1395 (~325px), charcoal rounded card, sections separated by hairlines, each option a row: label left, '?' circle right, slider + numeric field below; step rail x=1395–1440 with numbers 1–7 stacked at the top and the vertical 'UNIVERSAL SANS' tab at the bottom; top bar 30px
reconstruction.typography: Sample 202px Universal Sans Display GX (wght 450, rnds 50, xhgt 40, prop 50, trml 0, skew 25), leading 1.04, tracking -0.008em, white; panel title ~11px caps; panel body ~13px Universal Sans Regular grey-white; slider labels ~13px; values ~12px
reconstruction.behaviour: Panel slides in from the right after load and the sample text types itself on (storyboard t≈1.6–4.3s); range inputs (wght 100–900; width/proportions/terminals/ink traps 0–100; x-height 0–80) write font-variation-settings on every .font--update element; alternate tiles set ss01–ss20 / cv09–cv19; selections serialise into the BuildID (e.g. #v2.0.0.50.25.40.50.1111111111111111111.01.01.450) in the URL hash; step rail scrolls the panel to that step
reconstruction.content: Instructional copy per step ('Welcome to Universal Sans, the award-winning customisable typeface platform…'); sample 'Hello font friend.'
reconstruction.assets: Variable fonts with custom axes (UniversalSansGX, DisplayGX, ItalicDisplayGX); no imagery
reconstruction.html: div.section--instruct > div#instruct--N.instruct--block[data-section=N] > div.header.panel--title + div.instruct--panel rows with input[type=range][name=amountRange]; div.instruct--selector > .selector--basic / .selector--advanced; span.build--number

instances.look: The configurator's stage: one editable sample at 202px with a dark pill toolbar along the bottom (Opentype, TT size slider with '202px' readout, leading 'A/A 3.8', tracking 'VA -4.1', Text | Display segmented switch, Auto, black/white half-circle toggle, It, AA, vertical-centre and three alignment buttons) and a row of content pills above it (Abc, Word, Sentence, Paragraph, Glyphs)
instances.ux: Click and type in the sample; size slider 12–500px; leading and tracking are editable numbers with up/down arrows; Opentype opens a list of 13 feature toggles (calt, case, dnom, frac, locl, nalt, numr, ordn, sinf, subs, sups, tnum, zero); content pills swap the text for an alphabet, a word, a sentence, a paragraph or the glyph sheet; the axis sliders live in the side panel
instances.learn: Separate 'what the font is' (axes in the side panel) from 'how I am looking at it' (size, spacing, case, colour, text preset in a bottom toolbar), so the preview controls never mix with the design choices

instances.look: Behind the INTERPOLATOR tab of step 1 (HTML only, not visible in the capture): a square 10×10 grid pad with a crosshair (x line labelled 'rnds 50', y line 'wght 450') and a dot at the current value, above two dropdowns choosing which axis drives X and which drives Y

instances.learn: Let visitors choose which two axes the pad maps, so one small control explores every pair in a six-axis design space

instances.look: The 'Glyphs' preset of the stage (HTML only): a flex grid of ~375 cells, each with the character as a small label on top, the glyph rendered in the current build, and its code point (U+0041) at the bottom

instances.learn: Render the glyph sheet in the visitor's own configuration: the character set becomes a check of their choices, not a static catalogue

instances.look: Step 7 'Download your family' in the side panel and a checkout section (HTML only): a Trial option with 'I agree to the EULA', licence selects (Desktop by personnel 1 → >640, Web by visitors <2.5k → >2m, Social by followers…), then Billing details, Licence holder, Payment (Stripe) and a 'Review order' table: Licence 450 Weights £75.00, Italics +50%, Text & Display +50%, Custom Name +25%, Total

instances.learn: Price the custom build as a base licence plus percentage surcharges for each extra (italics, Text+Display, custom name) so the cost visibly follows the visitor's choices
